The rain drummed a relentless, hollow rhythm against the windowpane of the cramped apartment, but Elias barely heard it. The room smelled of stale coffee and the metallic tang of the radiator, a scent that had become the backdrop of his existence.

He sat on the edge of the mattress, his hands trembling slightly as he laid out the small, crinkled plastic baggie. For a moment, he just stared at it. It was a tiny, unassuming thing, yet it held the gravity of his entire world. The silence in the room felt heavy, pressing against his chest, a physical weight he had been trying to escape for months.

He moved with a practiced, mechanical efficiency. There was no ceremony left in the ritual, only the desperate, singular focus of a man trying to stop the shaking. When he finally leaned back against the peeling wallpaper, he closed his eyes and let out a long, shuddering breath.
